eocene: from 58 million to 40 million years ago
eocene epoch: from 58 million to 40 million years ago
eolian: a member of one of four linguistic divisions of the prehistoric Greeks
eolic: the dialect of Ancient Greek spoken in Thessaly and Boeotia and Aeolis
eolith: a crude stone artifact (as a chipped flint)
eolithic: the earliest part of the Stone Age marked by the earliest signs of human culture
of or relating to the earliest period of the Stone Age (characterized by the use of eoliths)
eolithic age: the earliest part of the Stone Age marked by the earliest signs of human culture
eolotropic: having properties with different values along different axes
eon: the longest division of geological time
an immeasurably long period of time
eonian: of or relating to a geological eon (longer than an era)
eoraptor: a theropod dinosaur of the genus Eoraptor
eos: (Greek mythology) the winged goddess of the dawn in ancient mythology
eosin: a red fluorescent dye resulting from the action of bromine on fluorescein
eosinopenia: a decrease in the number of eosinophils in the blood
eosinophil: a leukocyte readily stained with eosin
eosinophile: a leukocyte readily stained with eosin
